description:
FOUND s496a (Opus, 2026-09-26): a FLAKY gate row, pre-existing (reproduced on a b6560c21 extraction).

Pl/t/glob-01.t rows 29-30 ('glob result can be filtered with grep') build `grep { /\/a\.txt$/ } <$tmpdir/*.txt>` with File::Temp's RANDOM directory name.  When that name contains a digit followed by m / s / y / q (a quote-like operator letter) -- e.g. /tmp/IxJITznB9m -- PPI 1.291 lexes the `<` after the grep BLOCK's `}` as a less-than OPERATOR, then `/tmp/IxJITznB` as a MATCH, `9` as a Number and `m/*.txt>;` as another match, and PCL drops the statement ("Bug. Fell through. Missing case: [..., 'Token::Number<9>']").  The gate reads FAIL on those runs (measured once in s496a's final gate; four re-runs passed).

Minimal reproducer (no randomness):
    my @f = grep { /x/ } </tmp/a9m/*.txt>; print scalar(@f), "\n";
  perl: 0      PCL: "PCL: statement dropped ..." then dies
  Probed: a9m a2m x9m a9s drop; a9x a9mb aB9 a9b ab a1 do not.  `my @f = </tmp/aB9m/*.txt>;` (no grep block) does not drop.

TWO things to do: (1) the PPI mis-lex -- log it in docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md + docs/ppi-bug-report.t (CLAUDE.md rule 13) and repair it in the token-repair pass (a `<` right after a BLOCK-arg `}` of grep/map/sort that closes with `>` before the statement end is a glob); (2) the test's non-determinism -- until (1) lands the row passes or fails by the random name, so no single gate run tells either way.

=== s543d (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21; the repair-pass audit, docs/ppi-fix-at-source-s527.md §10) ===
VERDICT: the task's own reproducer = perl 5.40.3 on main 64353611 (and on the s543d tree) -- PROBE, scratch/s543d/p4/a02 (`grep { /x/ } <a9m/*.txt>`, a directory name holding a digit then m).  FIXED by PCL's PPI group AH (s527d, §14: after a block a closed `<...>` is one Readline).  Closable once a guard row in a Pl/t file holds the reproducer (PPI batch 12, member 4 of the proposed list: "the closes, with guard rows only").

=== DONE (s543f) ===
CLOSED BY A GUARD ROW, no code: `grep { /x/ } <DIR/*.txt>` with a directory name holding a digit then m / s / y / q is ONE Readline on PCL's PPI since group AH (s527d, §14: after a block a closed `<...>` is a readline), = perl on main ffc7eb72 and the s543f tree.  Guard (deterministic, no random name): Pl/t/readline-ternary-01.t "#651 / #2384: <./g-[ab].t> after sort, and <./a9m/*.txt> after a grep block" (an `a9m` directory in the fixture).
Pl/t/glob-01.t rows 29-30 are NOT name-dependent any more: with File::Temp's directory forced under names of the failing kind (TMPDIR = a9m, x2s, b7y, c3q: a digit then m / s / y / q), rows 29-30 PASS on main 55e5cdd4 and on the s543f tree, 8 of 8 runs (scratch/s543f/legs/glob2384b.log in the s543f worktree).
CLOSE-WITH-ROWS: no baseline / skip-registry / not-supported / STATUS row is keyed on #2384.


=== CLOSED at MAIN-READY-105 `8ef15927` (the reviewing session, 2026-11-22; s543f = PPI batch 11 merged; gate on merged main 380 files / 12,397 rows PASS) -- the guard row named in the DONE block above is in the gate; no baseline row is keyed on this task (the hits for the number in baselines/ are a row number, perl's own test label and a history comment).
subject: FLAKY gate row (pre-existing): Pl/t/glob-01.t 29-30 fail when File::Temp`s random dir name has a digit then m/s/y/q -- PPI lexes `grep { ... } </tmp/a9m/*.txt>` as < operator + regex + number + m//, and the statement drops
triage_reason: a flaky gate row caused by a PPI mis-lex (the PPI branch)
